To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

Inês,

I’m so sorry to leave you with this, especially with the Figure 3 error surfacing so late. My father is ill, and I’m with my family. I don’t know yet how long I’ll be away.

I trust you completely to lead the launch. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the Annex B sensitivity analyses yourself. And please remember Lisbon: when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel without missing a beat. You’re better live than you think.

The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks how it happened, please say so. You shouldn’t have to carry it.

I’ve put the urgent things first below. This is a lot to hand over at once, but the immediate priority is making sure the corrected number reaches Hanna and the journalists before the embargo lifts.

1. Correct the press release and tell the journalists

Please contact Hanna first. The embargoed release she sent to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday says EUR 2.1 billion for 2030. The correct LDC-relevant revenue estimate is EUR 1.4 billion. The old figure came from a run that had not applied the free-allocation phase-out.

Ask her to prepare and send a corrected release to everyone who received the original, making the correction clear, before the embargo lifts on Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. If Hanna needs a senior name to sign it off, Geert knows I’m away and can sign off the corrected release.

The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does. Please don’t let the old figure circulate without an explicit correction.

Hanna had also told two journalists I would be available for background calls on Wednesday afternoon: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar has calls at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each, with Hanna to confirm. Please agree with her who will take them and have her confirm the arrangements with the journalists. They should have the corrected figure before or during those conversations, with the correction clearly explained.

2. Update the presentation

PDF v7 on the drive is corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Please use that as the reference version for the launch.

Deck v4 still needs the correction on slides 6 and 9; slide 9 has the revenue chart. Please check both the visible slides and the speaker notes for the old number, and make sure the chart and any accompanying text match PDF v7. Use EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion, for the 2030 LDC-relevant estimate.

The deck is 14 slides, but Tomás has asked us to cut the presentation from 20 to 15 minutes because Katarina’s vote has moved. Please trim it however you think best. You know what the audience needs; you don’t need to preserve my wording or notes. I’d make the corrected estimate and the paper’s main conclusion clear, then leave enough time for the panel.

3. Confirm the revised event plan with Tomás

Tomás’s latest email changes the run of show in the folder. The presentation should start at 12:35 and run for 15 minutes, with the panel starting at 12:50. Katarina has to leave at 13:30 and wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes.

Please confirm with Tomás how he and Katarina want to handle those questions and the moderation after she leaves, including the rest of the Q&A and the 14:00 close. The older run of show has Q&A at 13:40, so we need an agreed plan rather than relying on that version. Please also confirm that you will present and take my place on the panel.

Tomás needs the final names of everyone attending from our side by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00. Please send him the list by then and check he has what he needs for you. Guests need to be at the European Parliament security entrance by 12:00 on Thursday; Tomás is collecting the badges. The event is in the Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Katarina’s office. Light lunch is outside the room from 12:00.

Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite; she tested it last week and it worked. Please check with Tomás who is handling the remote connection on the day and make sure Abena has the updated timing.

4. Panel and questions

Please lead with the paper’s question and findings, rather than letting Florian Kessler make the event a referendum on the 80% pass-through assumption. He has said he will raise that assumption and the risk of resource shuffling.

On pass-through, be open about what we did: 80% is the central case. Annex B tests 60% and 40%; the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. You ran those analyses, so please explain them in the way that feels clearest to you. There’s no need to be defensive or to claim the result holds equally at every assumption.

On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk. Section 5.2 addresses it, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Abena may also bring a useful LDC perspective, but let her speak for herself.

If the correction comes up, say plainly that the previous 2030 figure was based on the old run without the free-allocation phase-out, that the corrected figure is EUR 1.4 billion, and that I made the mistake. The paper’s conclusion is unchanged. Please don’t minimise the correction: it changes the headline number.

5. After the event

Lucy Tran and a colleague are attending. For the Halvorsen grant report, Lucy has asked for two event photos and the attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please arrange for someone to take the photos and capture the attendance count on Thursday, then send them to her by that date if possible. If someone else can handle this, please delegate it.

You can call me if you need me. After 09:00 tomorrow I might not pick up, so please don’t wait for me if a decision needs to be made. Use your judgement, and bring Geert in if you need senior cover.

I’m sorry again for the late correction and for leaving you to put the pieces together. Thank you for taking this on. I know you can do it, and I trust you to make it yours.

Marieke
